pr_title: HttpSys log correct statuscode when application throws
pr_body:
# HttpSys log correct statuscode when application throws

`application.DisposeContext` should be called after setting the status code when an application exception is thrown.
This is also mentioned in Kestrel:
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/8897c2947e985fbfcea06ed67427dc10644024e0/src/Servers/Kestrel/Core/src/Internal/Http/HttpProtocol.cs#L728-L730

Fixes #42218
pr_comments: Thanks for your PR, @campersau. Someone from the team will get assigned to your PR shortly and we'll get it reviewed.
Can this be unit-tested? It's subtle behavior and easy to regress.

I have added a test for Kestrel and HttpSys but I am not sure if that is the correct location for it.
It might also get flaky as it has to wait a bit for the server to finish the request. (See Task.Delay).

issue_context.title: Unhandled exception in request still logs `Request finished ... 200`
issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

Using the HttpSys server, an unhandled exception from the request pipeline causes the logging to log "request finished with 200 OK", but the request returns the expected 500 to the browser.

This behavior is particularly bad when paired with application insights logging. The app insights logs contain a "successful" request telemetry, when this request actually failed.

Example Log:
```
...
Application started. Press Ctrl+C to shut down.
info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[1]
      Request starting HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - -
fail: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.HttpSysListener[6]
      ProcessRequestAsync
      System.Exception: Exception of type 'System.Exception' was thrown.
         at aspnetrepro.Startup.<>c.<Configure>b__1_0(HttpContext ctx, Func`1 next) in D:\aspnetrepro\aspnet-bad-request-log\Program.cs:line 41
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder.UseExtensions.<>c__DisplayClass0_1.<Use>b__1(HttpContext context)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.HostingApplication.ProcessRequestAsync(Context context)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.RequestContext`1.ExecuteAsync()
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.HttpSys.RequestContext`1.ExecuteAsync()
info: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting.Diagnostics[2]
      Request finished HTTP/1.1 GET http://localhost:5000/ - - - 200 - - 39.6126ms
```

### Expected Behavior

All requests log the status code they actually return to the browser

### Steps To Reproduce

Clone this repo https://github.com/alexperovich/aspnet-bad-request-log, `dotnet run`, then open the browser.

### Exceptions (if any)

_No response_

### .NET Version

6.0.301
